metadata.subject: Science and Technology
metadata.description: UPSC Prelims Science & Technology question grammar dataset for few-shot prompting and style conditioning.

patterns.title: Concept Definition / Single-Choice
patterns.explanation: Tests core STEM concepts, definitions, and technology principles.

example_questions.question: Which one of the following best describes a semiconductor?
options: (a) A material with very high electrical conductivity
(b) A material with electrical conductivity between that of a conductor and an insulator
(c) A material that cannot conduct electricity at any temperature
(d) A superconducting material at room temperature
example_questions.pattern_notes: Tests basic physics/material science concept; distractors reflect common misunderstandings.

distractor_rationales.(c): False — semiconductors do conduct under conditions.
distractor_rationales.(d): Superconductors are different and not at room temperature.

patterns.title: Multi-Statement Evaluation
patterns.explanation: Evaluates multiple statements involving scientific facts or technology attributes.

example_questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Radio waves have shorter wavelength than X-rays.
2. Infrared radiation lies between visible light and microwaves.
3. Gamma rays have the highest frequency in the electromagnetic spectrum.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options: (a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 2 and 3 only
(c) 1 and 3 only
(d) All three
example_questions.pattern_notes: Tests understanding of electromagnetic spectrum ordering.

distractor_rationales.(a): Statement 1 is incorrect (radio waves longer than X-rays).

patterns.title: Match-the-Pair
patterns.explanation: Tests association between technologies and applications or scientists and discoveries.

example_questions.question:
Match the following:
List I
1. CRISPR
2. LIGO
3. GPS

List II
(a) Gravitational wave detection
(b) Genome editing technology
(c) Satellite-based positioning system
Select the correct answer:
example_questions.pattern_notes: Associates modern technology names with applications.

patterns.title: Assertion–Reason Type
patterns.explanation: Tests linkage between scientific cause and effect or principles.

example_questions.question:
Assertion (A): 5G technology offers higher data rates than 4G.
Reason (R): 5G uses higher frequency bands compared to 4G.
Which of the following is correct?
options: (a) Both A and R are correct and R explains A
(b) Both A and R are correct but R does not explain A
(c) A is correct but R is incorrect
(d) Both are incorrect
example_questions.pattern_notes: Tests cause–effect between technology upgrade and frequency utilization.

distractor_rationales.(b): R does explain A (higher frequency → more bandwidth).

patterns.title: Application / Data Interpretation
patterns.explanation: Tests ability to interpret simple scientific data or apply principles to scenarios.

example_questions.question: An astronaut in space experiences weightlessness because:
options: (a) There is no gravity in space
(b) The astronaut is moving too fast
(c) The astronaut is in free fall around Earth
(d) Earth’s gravity is zero at orbital height
example_questions.pattern_notes: Common physics application question; distractors reflect typical misconceptions.

patterns.title: Current-Linked Tech MCQ
patterns.explanation: Uses recent technology context to test foundational concepts.

example_questions.question: Recent advancements in quantum computing emphasize qubit coherence. What is a qubit in this context?
options: (a) A classical binary bit
(b) A quantum bit that can exist in superposition
(c) A data packet in networks
(d) A hardware register in CPUs
example_questions.pattern_notes: Links current research discussion with basic quantum computing concepts.

distractor_rationales.(d): Hardware register is not a qubit.
